second_order: calling for JoJo marks on the canvas
theme_note: These codes all solicit visible JoJo work on r/place; what varies is whether the call is a broad request, a named motif, a coordinate, help for an active build, or a proposal to negotiate for room.

second_order: routing posts into the right thread
theme_note: These moderation turns direct scattered requests or joke posts into an existing coordination or Dojyaaan thread; the destination and subject vary.

second_order: posting and outing a fake Part 5 promo
theme_note: The post performs the subreddit own April Fools joke and the reply names it as April Fools; this is not canvas conduct.

second_order: working from guides, coordinates, and fill order
theme_note: These codes turn a desired mark into a workable placement by choosing a feasible sign, testing locations, following a guide, setting coordinates, and deciding what to fill first.

second_order: joining, sticking with, and redeploying between builds
theme_note: These codes enact participation rather than merely propose it: people join, promise persistence, locate the work, thank helpers, put the group first, or move to another build after finishing; commitment varies from short-term help to staying until bored.

second_order: avoiding overwriting neighbours and negotiating room
theme_note: These codes respond to shared-space collisions by checking borders, moving, contacting neighbours, reading their plans, or reporting help and treaties; outcomes range from worry and proposed relocation to an official agreement.

second_order: taking canvas coordination to Discord
theme_note: These codes move part of the work off Reddit through a Discord invite and PlaceWorldCouncil diplomacy; one opens access while the other reports what returned from the unseen venue.

second_order: answering a WRYYYY request with a gift
theme_note: This single code is a playful response offering a gift while wondering whether the request belongs in Dojyaaan; it does not fit the building or moderation practices.

second_order: turning the sub into Love Live Crusaders
theme_note: These codes make, enforce, explain, celebrate, and eventually police the moderator-declared Love Live-only theme; what varies is whether people announce the switch, invoke the rule, explain April 1, ask JoJo posters to wait, or mark content as off-theme.

second_order: mashing Love Live and JoJo together
theme_note: These posts keep the subreddit joke going by joining the two fandoms in names, openings, characters, fights, ranks, and edited images; the specific mash-up changes but the practice is making each franchise speak through the other.

second_order: playing the Love Live theme straight
theme_note: These codes participate by posting, praising, ranking, or sharing Love Live material without necessarily combining it with JoJo; they vary from clips and fanart to best-girl judgments.

second_order: reacting to the April Fools change
theme_note: These codes step outside or comment on the performance by asking why the fandoms are united, choosing between them, joking about waking up, comparing expected parodies, praising the maker, or asking to repeat the joke.

second_order: posting April Fools announcements and hoaxes
theme_note: These codes imitate news or official announcements during the subreddit joke; what varies is a death hoax, a new idol series, Part 5 news, or a leaked opening.

second_order: showing the joke to the Love Live Reddit
theme_note: This single code takes the subreddit performance to the Love Live Reddit and reports its unexpectedly positive reception.

second_order: losing, rebuilding, and defending canvas work
theme_note: Participants report pixel work being destroyed, unfinished, reborn, contributed to, and harder to defend than expected; what varies is whether the immediate limit is erasure, too few people, or the labour of holding the image.

second_order: removing a pixel-art post under the fanart-title rule
theme_note: A moderator removes one JoJo pixel-art Discord post because its title lacks the required fanart tag; this is a single-code administrative practice and does not establish how organizers used the Discord.

second_order: stopping proposals when placement ends
theme_note: A participant answers an active image proposal by stating that r/place ended an hour earlier and the room is too late; this single-code practice closes pixel placement rather than explaining why earlier builds failed.

second_order: making sense of the finished canvas
theme_note: A participant asks what the now-fixed pixel collage is, beginning a post-event practice of interpreting what remained rather than coordinating new placement.

second_order: thanking people for the JoJo spot
theme_note: After placement ends, participants show the final product, open appreciation, thank contributors, value being beside Love Live, and claim recognition on the first community canvas; what varies is whether they foreground the artifact, its neighbour, or collective credit.

second_order: arguing over who covered whom
theme_note: Participants complain that Stranger Things covered Honoka, correct the order by saying the other work was there first, and recast the covered version as cuter; the practice joins blame, chronological correction, and aesthetic accommodation.

second_order: mistaking an ordinary place for an r/place request
theme_note: Moderator automation routes a chapter-source post as though its ordinary use of place were a canvas-image request; this single-code error differs from the otherwise purposeful coordination redirects.

second_order: missing a fight after a chapter source mess-up
theme_note: A participant says a source error made them miss the Oyecomova fight; this single-code ordinary manga-reading practice is retained because the thread became an r/place moderation episode, but it does not belong with canvas coordination.
